subject: Private offer duration ladder and pricing smoothing — DataWave pilot
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@datawave.com>
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2028-05-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private offer duration ladder and pricing smoothing — DataWave pilot

Hi Alicia —

Great talking earlier. Per our call, DataWave is targeting a pilot that spans existing fiscal quarters and procurement wants a clear activation/renewal cadence that won't trigger a full RFP. Two ideas to unblock approvals on your side:

1) Term staircase: start with a 6-month pilot with an option to extend to 12 months at a pre-agreed discount band, then 24 months for production. This lets budget owners sign the 6-month pilot faster while preserving price protection if you scale.

2) Pricing smoothing: spread the effective cost across the first 12 months for procurement reporting (i.e., amortized sticker) while reserving usage-tier credits for actual consumption spikes. This helps CFO/CPO teams reconcile the pilot without a lump-sum hit.

Attached is a short pricing-smoothing proposal and an ROI model that maps the three-term outcome to your forecast. If procurement is comfortable, we can route a private offer that includes the staircase terms and a DocuSign-ready MOP (managed offer page) for quick activation.

Next steps — could you share who on procurement and finance needs to sign off? If helpful, I can draft a one-page approval note they can attach to the PO.

Thanks,
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: DataWave_ROI_model.xlsx, pricing-smoothing-proposal.pdf

From: Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@datawave.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@datacloud.com
Date: 2028-05-09T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer duration ladder and pricing smoothing — DataWave pilot

Sofia —

Thanks for the outline and the files. The staircase concept looks promising; procurement is worried about multi-year commitments without clear delivery gates. A few quick asks from our side:

- Can the 6 -> 12 -> 24 month escalation be tied to a simple acceptance criteria (uptime / latency SLO + usage threshold)?
- For the pricing smoothing, procurement wants language that the amortized cost is for internal accounting only and that invoices will still match usage unless we opt into a committed spend.
- Who signs the private offer? Our procurement lead (procurement@datacloud.com) will need a redline-ready doc for legal.

I'll loop procurement and finance if you can provide: (1) a one-page approver summary, (2) a redlineable private-offer template, and (3) the ROI sheet with conservative usage assumptions.

Best,
Alicia
Alicia Torres
Head of Product Operations | DataWave
Alicia.Torres@DataWave.com

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@datawave.com>
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2028-05-09T13:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer duration ladder and pricing smoothing — DataWave pilot

Alicia —

Thanks — good asks. Quick answers inline and attaching the one-pager and a private-offer draft you can redline.

- Acceptance criteria: yes — we propose two gates: (a) pilot completion (6 months) with a joint ops review confirming <5% p99 tail latency deviations and >80% of predicted ingestion rate; (b) scale trigger: sustained 30% above forecasted average daily token usage for two consecutive weeks. We'll add these to the MOP.
- Accounting language: we can add a clause that specifies the "amortized price" is for internal accounting and invoices will default to meter-based billing unless a committed spend addendum is signed.
- Signatory and redlines: typically procurement signs the PO and legal signs the MSA amendment. We'll put a DocuSign-ready MOP and a redlineable private-offer doc in the bundle.

I attached: approver-summary.pdf (one page), private-offer-draft.docx (track-changes friendly), and an updated ROI modeling sheet with a conservative usage scenario.

If procurement wants, Vanessa can join the call with your procurement lead to walk through approval language. What does your team's availability look like tomorrow morning?

Cheers,
Sofia

Attachments: approver-summary.pdf, private-offer-draft.docx, DataWave_ROI_model.xlsx (updated)

From: procurement@datacloud.com
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>, Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@datawave.com>
Date: 2028-05-10T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer duration ladder and pricing smoothing — DataWave pilot

Hi Sofia / Alicia —

Procurement here. Appreciate the materials. A few clarifications before we put this on the purchasing calendar:

- The CFO will require an explicit cancellation clause that limits financial exposure if the vendor fails to meet the acceptance criteria. Can you propose a capped liability or pro-rated refund mechanism for the pilot period?
- We need to know the invoicing cadence and whether Redwood can accept a PO with a T&Cs reference rather than fully executed MSA on day 0.
- Please confirm whether private-offer activation can be staged (activate sandbox billing first, then production) and how that maps to buyer approval lanes in AWS Marketplace.

If you can get answers by EOD today, we can slot this for the Tuesday purchasing review.

Thanks,
Procurement Team | DataWave
procurement@datacloud.com

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
To: procurement@datacloud.com, Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@datawave.com>
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2028-05-11T16:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer duration ladder and pricing smoothing — DataWave pilot

Team —

Following up with specifics so you have material for the purchasing review:

1) Cancellation and liability: we can add a pilot failure clause that provides a pro-rated credit on prepaid committed amounts for the pilot window if agreed acceptance criteria are not met. We generally cap liability per the MSA at the contract value, but for the pilot we can add a hard cap equal to the pilot committed spend (i.e., refundable portion only). We'll add the exact phrasing to the private-offer draft.

2) Invoicing cadence and PO acceptance: Redwood accepts a PO referencing the MOP + private-offer ID for activation. Invoices can be monthly and align to actual usage unless you elect to prepay the pilot amount, in which case we will issue a single prepaid invoice and apply the refund mechanism above if the pilot fails.

3) Staged activation: yes — AWS Marketplace supports staged activation. We can create the private offer with a "sandbox" entitlement that triggers test metering; production entitlement will be enabled upon mutual acceptance after the pilot gate. We'll document the activation steps in the approver summary and the MOP.

Action items: Vanessa to set up a 30-minute review with your procurement lead and finance to confirm wording and the DocuSign path. I will circulate an updated private-offer-draft (track changes) and the approver-summary with the added refund/cap language before the call.

Proposed times: Tue 2028-05-13 08:00-08:30 PT or 10:00-10:30 PT. Which works for your team?

Thanks,
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: signed-mop-draft.docx, pricing-smoothing-proposal.pdf
